content.text:
The search results don't directly address oauth2-proxy, but the issue is very clear from the logs. Let me update the ticket with my findings.

Based on my investigation, I have identified the root cause of the login failures. The error logs from the oauth2-proxy pod clearly show that the Azure client secret has expired, preventing successful OAuth2 token exchange with Azure AD.

input.note:
Root Cause: The Azure client secret for the ops portal's app registration (ID: 6c2e9a41-58d3-4b7f-a0e2-91d4f3c87b15) has expired.

Evidence: The oauth2-proxy logs contain repeated errors starting at 2026-05-21 08:01:37 showing "AADSTS7000222: The provided client secret keys for app are expired" with subsequent 500 errors when users attempt to complete OAuth2 callback after successful Microsoft sign-in.

Fix: Since the ticket notes that the app registration is owned by the IT identity team, contact them to generate a new client secret in the Azure portal. Once a new secret is created, update the Kubernetes secret in the internal-tools namespace that the oauth2-proxy deployment references (specified in --client-secret-file=/etc/oauth2-proxy/client-secret). The oauth2-proxy will use the updated secret on its next request after the secret is updated.
